title: Several product images on the homepage fail to load (403 / ORB-blocked from media-stage.thekanaa.com)
preconditions: Guest session, homepage loaded, scrolled so the affected widget is in view.
stepsToReproduce: Go to https://dev-nx.thekanaa.com/en-sa/
Scroll to the "Big adventures start with small steps" widget (and others — see notes).
Observe several product tiles show a broken-image placeholder instead of the product photo.
expectedResult: Every product tile shows its product photo.
actualResult: 5 images consistently fail across two independent test runs (initial discovery and later execution): Maisto Rock Crawler R/C Car, Maisto 1:24 1929 Ford Model A, Maisto 1:24 1967 Ford Mustang GT, Disney Stitch Light-Up Yoyo, Pop Mart Labubu keychain — plus 2 non-product thirdlevelbanner images. Each fails with either a 403 from the site's own /_next/image proxy or net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB fetching the source directly from media-stage.thekanaa.com — same asset, same failure, both paths. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-09-14, direct S3 probe): each affected image URL returns HTTP 403 from S3 itself with body AccessDenied (not NoSuchKey) — the object exists but its S3 ACL/bucket-policy does not grant public read for these specific keys, while sibling objects in the same bucket (e.g. .../5/4/5432721578st2100082_1.jpg) return 200 with no query-string changes needed. The Next.js /_next/image proxy is working correctly — it detects the bad upstream and returns its own 403 ("upstream response is invalid"), it is not the source of the problem. This also explains why raw-URL vs proxied-URL and with/without resize query params made no difference: the object itself is unreadable at the S3 layer, independent of how the app requests it.
reproducibility: Always (reproduced identically across 2 independent full test runs, several hours apart)
notes: RECOMMENDED FIX (infra/ops, not app code): re-apply the public-read ACL / bucket policy to these 5 S3 objects (and audit for any other objects from the same upload batch) on the media-stage.thekanaa.com bucket — likely a recent product-import batch used a different upload credential/ACL default than the rest of the catalog. Separately (unrelated to the fix): a wider set of product images intermittently showed naturalWidth=0 in later, longer automated test runs — not bundled into this bug, matches this project's documented IP-based throttling behavior (README.md) rather than a distinct defect; re-verify with an isolated fresh run before filing separately.

title: Homepage triggers a cross-origin prefetch to production thekanaa.com that fails CORS, on every load
preconditions: Fresh guest session, no ad blocker.
stepsToReproduce: Open browser devtools console and network tab.
Go to https://dev-nx.thekanaa.com/en-sa/ and let it fully load (no further interaction needed).
expectedResult: No console errors on a clean homepage load; all first-party requests stay on dev-nx.thekanaa.com (or the site's own CDN) and succeed.
actualResult: A React Server Component prefetch for the "Pools & Outdoor" category redirects from dev-nx.thekanaa.com to the production apex domain thekanaa.com, which has no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header for that request — the browser blocks it, logging a CORS console error and a net::ERR_FAILED network failure. Reproduced identically on every one of 3 independent test runs.
notes: Likely an environment-config mismatch (a category redirect target still pointing at prod instead of dev-nx/mcstaging) rather than an application bug — worth routing to whoever owns the dev-nx environment config alongside the fix.

title: mcstaging.thekanaa.com returns 503 for multiple homepage-linked pages; one link to it is additionally malformed
stepsToReproduce: GET https://mcstaging.thekanaa.com/en-sa/about-us -> 503
GET https://mcstaging.thekanaa.com/en-sa/toys-games/dolls-collectables.html?page=1 -> 503 (linked from the "Big adventures start with small steps" widget)

Separately: inspect the "Ready set go" widget's DOM for a link with href="https:/mcstaging.thekanaa.com/en-sa/about-us" (single slash) — confirmed via a live browser check that this exact malformed href resolves to https://dev-nx.thekanaa.com/mcstaging.thekanaa.com/en-sa/about-us (a broken same-origin path) instead of the intended host.
expectedResult: Linked mcstaging pages return 200, and every href is a well-formed absolute URL.
actualResult: Two different mcstaging.thekanaa.com paths return 503 (reproduced across 2 runs); one homepage link to that host is malformed and would mis-navigate in a real browser.
reproducibility: Always for the 503s (2/2 runs); the malformed href is static markup, not load-dependent
notes: The malformed-href link is currently hidden (display:none, no accessible name) — low real-world impact on its own, but worth fixing alongside the 503s since both point at the same subdomain. Node's URL parser normalizes the single-slash form leniently, which is why this was initially missed by an HTTP-only check — confirmed instead via a live Chromium a.href evaluation.

title: QA/placeholder test products render live in homepage product widgets
preconditions: None — visible on a guest homepage load, content depends on widget rotation.
stepsToReproduce: Load the homepage and scroll through the product widgets (may require more than one load, since widget content rotates).
Look for a product tile named "Testing product for label" or "Rental Test Product".
expectedResult: Only real, purchasable catalog products appear in homepage widgets.
actualResult: Two placeholder/test products were found rendering as ordinary tiles in live homepage widgets during discovery.
reproducibility: Observed once at discovery time; widget content rotates so a fixed repro isn't guaranteed on demand
notes: Catalog/CMS data-hygiene issue, not a code defect — route to whoever owns product/CMS content review.

title: A homepage product widget has a blank section title
preconditions: Guest session; scroll to the widget between "Deals Of The Week" and "Most Popular Products".
stepsToReproduce: Load the homepage and scroll to the product widget located between "Deals Of The Week" and "Most Popular Products" (~5538px down the page at discovery time).
Observe the widget renders its product row with no heading/title text above it.
expectedResult: Every product widget shows a title describing its contents.
actualResult: This widget consistently renders with an empty heading, reproduced on every run (it cannot be re-verified by heading text for that reason, so every execution against it is recorded FAIL by design — see agents/homepage-executor.md).
reproducibility: Always (reproduced on every run so far)

retestHistory.note: Still failing (1/1): TC-HOME-043: Untitled widget — see known-risks.json RISK-HOME-001 (blank section heading).

title: Header search box's suggestions request fails (404)
stepsToReproduce: Click the header search box.
Type "toys".
Open devtools console.
expectedResult: Search suggestions load without error (or the feature degrades silently with no console error).
actualResult: Console logs "Error fetching suggestions" backed by a structured ApiError object: {name: "ApiError", message: "Index magento2_stagingen_sa_products_query_suggestions does not exist", status: 404}. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-09-14): the site's search backend (Magento 2 + an Elasticsearch/OpenSearch-based search module, judging by the index-name convention) is querying an index named magento2_stagingen_sa_products_query_suggestions for the en_sa storefront's autocomplete/query-suggestions feature, and that index does not exist on the staging search cluster — this is a missing-index/missing-reindex problem, not an application code bug.
reproducibility: Always (confirmed reproducible on demand, not just observed once — upgraded from the earlier "observed once" note)
notes: RECOMMENDED FIX (backend/DevOps, not app code): run the product query-suggestions indexer for the en_sa store view on the staging search cluster (Magento CLI equivalent of bin/magento indexer:reindex for the search/suggestions indexer, or whatever job creates magento2_stagingen_sa_products_query_suggestions) — likely this index was never created on staging, or a naming-convention change left staging pointing at a name that was never (re)built. This also explains why the CORS pooloutdoor issue (BUG-HOME-002) and this both surface early in a page load: both are calls made automatically on page load, unrelated to each other, that happen to land in the same console-listener window.

title: 8 homepage links have no accessible name
preconditions: Guest session, homepage loaded, screen reader or accessibility tree inspection.
stepsToReproduce: Load the homepage.
Inspect the accessibility tree (or use a screen reader) over the header logo link and the hero/category-widget banner links.
expectedResult: Every link exposes a non-empty accessible name (visible text, aria-label, or meaningful image alt).
actualResult: 8 visible links have no accessible name: the header logo link (href="/en-sa/"), several hero-banner slide links, and a handful of category-widget banner links (see evidence for the full href list).
reproducibility: Reproduced (same category of elements — header logo — every run; the exact widget-banner sample varies with content rotation)
notes: A screen reader user has no way to know what these links do before activating them. Adding aria-label (e.g. "Kanaa home") would resolve the header logo case immediately.

title: Two homepage section headings have malformed text
stepsToReproduce: Load the homepage.
Read the category-grid section heading: shows "Shop By Categorysssss".
Read the deals-widget section heading: shows "Best Price Guarante" (missing the final "e").
actualResult: Both headings are confirmed malformed via the accessibility tree (not just a visual/rendering artifact) — "Shop By Categorysssss" and "Best Price Guarante".
reproducibility: Always — static template text, confirmed on every run
notes: One product card badge was also observed reading "Best Pricee" (double e) during discovery — not included here since it's on a specific, dynamically-rotating product and wasn't re-confirmed on a later run; worth a spot-check if seen again.

retestHistory.note: Manual retest: Live-checked accessibility tree on 2026-09-14 — heading still reads literal text 'Best Price Guarante' (missing final e), unchanged
